text:
Sofia (People Ops): Hey team — quick q: we have an IC resigning effective 4/19 (mid-pay). They activated their HSA card but have pending reimbursements and want to reduce 401k pre-tax deferral on final paycheck. What's the process/cutoff? Any chance to push through HSA claims after termination? Thanks.

Marisa (Benefits): Short answer: HSA is employee-owned and portable — they keep the account. Card activity depends on vendor; typically the vendor may deactivate the card on the plan termination date (or immediately when we mark termination). Recommend they submit claims ASAP via the vendor portal. Claims for expenses incurred while covered are usually allowed after termination within the vendor's claims runout window (vendor-specific). We can't guarantee card transactions post-termination.

Ben - Payroll: For 401k deferral changes, payroll cutoff applies. Our standard cutoff for deferral/election changes is 48 hours before the payroll run (2 business days). If a change is submitted after cutoff it will apply to the next pay period. For a mid-month resignation we can sometimes process an off-cycle payroll to capture a deferral change, but that requires a payroll ticket + manager approval. Employer match is based on contributions actually withheld/paid, per the plan document.

Alex K: If they want to max the HSA for the year or do catch-up (50+), can payroll do an off-cycle to push more pre-tax into the HSA? Or any employer-side adjustment options?

Marisa (Benefits): We generally don't make retroactive employer HSA deposits except in rare, documented cases. Off-cycle HSA withholding can be done if payroll can run it before year-end, and the vendor accepts the deposit type. Catch-up contributions (50+) require the employee flagged correctly in payroll. Best practice: employee sets deferral before cutoff; if they miss cutoff, submit a payroll ticket for off-cycle with justification. Also, HSA claims for dates of service on or before termination are typically processable after termination (check vendor runout).

Ben - Payroll: Next steps for this case:
1) Employee submits 401k deferral change in the payroll portal and CCs benefits@redwood.com (if before cutoff it will apply to final paycheck).
2) If change is after cutoff, file a payroll ticket for an off-cycle with manager + HRBP approvals. Use this template:```
Subject: Off-cycle deferral request for [Employee Name], Emp ID [#####]
Reason: resignation effective [date] / request to change deferral for final pay
Approvals: Manager name, HRBP name
```
3) For HSA reimbursements: employee uploads receipts to the HSA vendor portal. If there are portal/card issues, open a ticket to benefits@redwood.com and include screenshots/transaction IDs.

BenefitsBot: Automated reminder — HSA claims with dates of service on or before termination are processable via the vendor portal. Standard claim runout is vendor-dependent (commonly ~90 days). Submit ASAP to avoid denial. :bell:

Sofia (People Ops): Thanks — I'll ping the employee and coordinate with Ben. One more thing: what paperwork do we send them for 401k rollover options when they separate?

Marisa (Benefits): After termination we send the 401k distribution/rollover packet within ~5 business days. Options we include: leave balance in plan (if eligible), direct rollover to their new employer's plan, rollover to an IRA, or cash out (tax implications + possible penalties). To initiate a direct rollover they complete the distribution form and provide trustee/account details. We also include an FAQ that explains taxes, timing, and contact info for the vendor.

Ben - Payroll: Note: final pay + accrued PTO are processed per the PTO policy and payroll schedule. 401k deferrals already withheld will be remitted per the payroll remittance schedule; any post-payroll corrections require documentation and may delay distribution.

Alex K: Super helpful — thanks all :thumbsup:

Sofia (People Ops): Action items for me: message employee with cutoff guidance, ask them to upload receipts and submit deferral change, and open payroll ticket if they miss cutoff. I'll cc benefits@redwood.com and the manager.

Marisa (Benefits): I'll standby to help with vendor outreach if the card is deactivated or claims are failing.

Ben - Payroll: I'll put a note in the payroll queue and confirm cutoff windows with the team — ping me if you need the off-cycle.

Sofia (People Ops): Closing this thread once I've confirmed with employee. Thanks everyone! :wave:
